title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
summary: The marginal degree of sums in dimension \(n\) is the smallest integer \(k\) such that the joint distributions of all subcollections of at most \(k\) coordinates of a real-valued random vector \(\left(X_1,\ldots,X_n\right)\) determine the value of \(\E\left(X_1+\cdots+X_n\right)\), whenever this expectation is defined. For every \(n\ge2\), we prove that this marginal degree is \(\left\lceil n/2\right\rceil\). The upper bound follows from a theorem of Simons (1977).
